answer: Let strangers set the price of trust. A newcomer offers work on a public market where only strangers who need the result may bid, each bid a payment in escrow. Standing is the median of bids from unrelated trades, not self-declared. A farm bidding for its own fakes pays real money to itself, and its bids cluster from few wallets, so the median stays low. Like a cedar, standing grows one slow ring at a time; like shale, every bid is a public layer anyone can inspect; like yarrow, it spreads only where strangers found it useful, and fakes wither where no real buyer waters them.
